toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The Android drop is not caused by release 6.14, the Android security patch, or bots. It comes from a new vendor rule. Corvane's rule pack 2026.03.1 went live on 3 March at 10:38 UTC. It includes rule AUTO-LIB-17, which blocks requests with the 'nettle-http' user-agent on the password-login path when there is no edge session cookie. The Android app uses that library for every API call. The rule returns HTTP 403 and has blocked about 9,600 requests a day. Those requests come from about 41,300 real installs, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected, because the rule never matches them.

The telemetry agrees. Password success fell from 96% to 8.2%, on every app version at once and starting within a minute of the rule going live. 6.14 is only 5% of attempts, so it can't explain a drop of this size. OS patch status made no difference. The extra failures are all server-side 403s, not wrong credentials, which also counters the claim that the new password screen is at fault.

Next steps: have Corvane set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits, lockout and all other rules active. Then confirm in telemetry that password success recovers. Don't roll back 6.14. Don't raise bot sensitivity. Don't remove blocked attempts from the KPI. Those would hide the problem or make it worse. I am fairly confident in this diagnosis. The call-volume link to the drop is plausible but unproven, because the fee mailing also fell in the same week.
